title: KYC update link vs. re-KYC reminder via official channels
summary: A caller from Kaveri Bank says the recipient's KYC details are due for update. In the fraud case, the caller sends a link, says the account will be frozen today unless the recipient fills it in, and asks for net-banking login details on that page. In the legitimate case, the caller reminds the recipient that periodic re-KYC is due and tells them to complete it at the branch or in the official app, with a deadline weeks away.

shared_setting.pretext: KYC (identity details) due for periodic update.
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult Kaveri Bank account holder; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers mention that accounts may face restrictions if KYC is not updated.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller directs the recipient to an unofficial link and asks for net-banking credentials there under a same-day threat.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to enter net-banking username and password on a look-alike page.
stable_facts: Link: https://kaveri-kyc-update.invalid/verify (sent by SMS during the call).
The page asks for customer ID, password, and then an OTP.

evidence.text: Caller tells the recipient to open the sent link and log in with net-banking ID and password
Caller says the account will be frozen today if not done

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller reminds the recipient of a routine requirement and directs them to official channels without asking for any credential or sending any link.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get the recipient to complete re-KYC before the due date.
stable_facts: Due date: four to six weeks away.
Options: use the "Update KYC" option in the official Kaveri Bank app they already have, or visit any branch with ID and address proof.
If nothing has changed in the customer's details, a self-declaration is enough.

cooperative.fraud: Says they are opening the link and asks which field to fill
cooperative.legitimate: Says they will do it in the app this week

clarifying.fraud: Asks why the bank's own app cannot be used instead
clarifying.legitimate: Asks which documents to bring to the branch

resistant.fraud: Says they will go to the branch and not open the link
resistant.legitimate: Says they are busy and will do it later

suspicious.fraud: Says the link looks fake and asks if this is a phishing call
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how they know this call is really from the bank

legitimate: recipient is told to verify by calling the number on their passbook or card.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may insist on the link or increase urgency. They must not switch to asking for payment or app installation. The legitimate caller must not send a link or request credentials after the branch.

must_preserve: weeks-away deadline and official channels in _L
may_vary: whether the recipient recently changed address
must_not_emit: the words "phishing" or "scam" in caller lines

ambiguities: Both cases mention KYC and possible account restrictions. The label depends on the link and credential request, not the topic.
A legitimate bank may send an SMS reminder. In this family the legitimate caller sends no link, so that link presence is a clean contrast. Legitimate SMS links belong in a different family if needed.

evidence_references.claim: Periodic KYC updating is required; with no change, self-declaration through bank channels suffices without a branch visit (C05)
Banks send advance reminders before the re-KYC due date (C06)
Calls threatening account blocking over KYC with a link are a common fraud (C04)
